helper_scripts: code/p3-dialogue-style-pb1_backtest.py (reused unchanged from pb1 so the whole cast is scored with one yardstick; not copied)
inputs_read: story/structured_story.json (+ shards ch001-ch012): dialogues[] with speaker labels (Mouse, Dodo, Bill, Caterpillar, Pigeon, Gryphon, Mock Turtle, Cook, Knave) and paragraph text for silent business (ch006, ch008, ch011-ch012)
bible/characters/index.json (IDs, tiers, performer concepts); all 9 IDs present
bible/h1_summary.md, bible/cultivation.json (SUP-002, SUP-004, SUP-010, SUP-014), runs/h1-ruling/ruling.json
schema: Same as pb1 so one script and one yardstick cover all cards: character_id, source_speaker_labels, register, catchphrases, sentence_style (length, mean_words, patterns[] each with 1-3 source examples as dialogue IDs chNNN-dNNNN), vocabulary, address, interjections, recitation_repertoire (verse), forbidden_words[] (domain + regex + reason, machine-checkable), drift[], backtest_markers[] (regex + weight + rule_ref), backtest{}. Rules and values beyond the source are tagged inferred:true + reason.

backtest_method.hit_rule: a spoken source line hits its speaker's card when it matches >= 1 backtest_markers[].regex AND none of forbidden_words[].regex (case-insensitive, curly quotes straightened, '_' emphasis and '[...]' elisions removed)
backtest_method.sample: 100% of the character's spoken lines (type dialogue/thought) under its source_speaker_labels; type verse (the Mouse's tale, the Mock Turtle's two songs) is excluded and listed in recitation_repertoire
backtest_method.width_guards: cross_claim_rate (share of the other 18 carded characters' lines this card would also claim), lift, and attribution_top1_rate (card has the unique top weighted score among all 19 cards). Informational; only hit_rate gates. All nine cards claim <= 4.8% of other speakers' lines, and top-1 attribution is 0.73-1.00
backtest_method.iteration: One tightening pass after the first run: the Mock Turtle card's bare 'of course' / ', you know' / 'explain' markers were shared by half the cast (cross-claim 9.5%); they were narrowed to his own forms ('Of course it was/not', 'explain all that', 'have it explained', 'explain it as you go', 'With what porpoise'), bringing cross-claim to 4.1% with hit rate unchanged at 1.0
backtest_method.for_dialogue_rewrite: run the same script with --lines <json list of {speaker_id, text}> on rewritten screenplay lines. Keep the Gryphon's dialect grammar and the Mock Turtle's genteel grammar apart: each card forbids the other's markers

key_decisions: Reused pb1's schema and back-test script instead of writing a second one, so the whole cast and dialogue-rewrite share one yardstick. I deleted a draft pb2 script before first use.

Small samples are reported, not padded. Bill has 1 source line, and the Cook and Knave have 2 each. Their 100% hit rates carry a small_sample_warning. Their silent scenes (Bill in the jury-box, the Cook in the kitchen, the Knave in the procession) are covered by rules tagged inferred:true that cap any added line at a few deferential or blunt words.
Shared chorus lines ('Wow! wow! wow!', label CHORUS) and unlabelled jurors are not counted as the Cook's or Bill's lines. The source never names those speakers.

Distinctiveness rules for the most-confusable pair. The Gryphon gets non-standard grammar, hurry-ups, 'old fellow', puns stated as fact, and impatience with explanation. The Mock Turtle gets grammatical, genteel nostalgia, school vocabulary, and demands for explanation. Each card's forbidden_words bans the other's signature forms.

Per SUP-002 every card treats the speaker as a human performer. The animal coding lives in what they talk about (nest and eggs, size, sea-school), never in animal noises. The Gryphon's 'Hjckrrh!' is a vocal cry. No card relies on narration (narration is off).
observations_for_other_agents: Adding nine cards changed the informational attribution_top1_rate of pb1's cards when the shared script is re-run (e.g. CHAR-alice 0.662 -> 0.550), because Alice's card and mine both claim some polite formulas. pb1 hit rates are unchanged (gate unaffected); pb1's own report file was not touched.

bible/characters/index.json lists CHAR-mouse gender as 'unspecified'. The source uses 'his tail' (ch002-p23), 'his story' (ch003-p48), and the card follows the source ('he'). This is not a style-card conflict. It is noted for character-manager/appearance, and no defect is filed.
